To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

worksite hypertension screenings do not increase overall absenteeism among heterogeneous workers but do increase absenteeism among some subgroups, and that antihypertension treatment decreases blood pressure in sustained hypertensive subjects.
worksite hypertension labeling does not significantly increase absenteeism rates in heterogeneous self-selected work force populations.

(1) worksite hypertension screening produces a significant increase in absenteeism in some subgroups of workers; (2) the increase is not statistically significant overall among heterogeneous workers, even with a high statistical power; (3) the increase may not be a consequence of hypertension screening per se but rather of the screening process and labeling; and (4) worksite hypertension labeling is followed by significant blood pressure lowering in the majority of subjects with sustained hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of worksite hypertension detection on absenteeism.
the effects of worksite hypertension (HTN) screening on the health of workers and on the productivity of the work place.
the consequences of worksite hypertension (HT) screening and labeling.
